newsitem.title: USA: Clinton names Hoecker to chair FERC.
newsitem.headline: Clinton names Hoecker to chair FERC.

text.p: The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission said Tuesday that President Clinton had named FERC member James Hoecker to chair the commission.
Hoecker, who has been a commissioner since 1993, replaces Elizabeth Moler as chair, following her departure Monday to become deputy energy secretary.
FERC is in the midst of overseeing the deregulation of the wholesale electricity market which has sparked a round of utility mergers.
"My colleagues and I will maintain our focus on the business at hand, even during this time of transition," Hoecker said in a statement.

The commission has five members appointed by the President and confirmed by the Senate who hold five-year terms. No more than three commissioners may belong to the same political party. Three commissioners are enough for the FERC to meet.

The departure of Moler and the pending departure of Commissioner Donald Santa will leave the commission with two Democrats -- Hoecker and Commissioner William Massey - and Republican Commissioner Vicky Bailey.
Massey, who was a leading contender to replace Moler as chair, Tuesday praised Hoecker and said he looked forward to continuing to work with him.
The top candidate to replace Santa is Mississippi Public Service Commission chairman Curt Hebert, who is being backed by Senate Republican leader Trent Lott of Mississippi.
Among the candidates mentioned as possible replacements for the open Democratic slot is Texas public utility commissioner Robert Gee.
